pool.text: The main port at Malindi, handling trade, was built.
Zanzibar introduced the first colour television service in sub-Saharan Africa.
The previous 45-megawatt cable was completed by Norway.
The government designated two export-producing zones and encouraged financial services.
Contested elections led to a violent massacre involving the army.
Violence erupted again after another contested election on the island.
A Norwegian consultancy firm went to determine potential oil development.
Political leaders met at the State House to discuss turmoil.
Voters adopted a proposal to amend the constitution for national unity.
The sinking of a ship became the worst disaster in history.
The Viscas Corporation of Japan began laying a cable.
The new subsea electrical cable became fully operational.
Christ Church Cathedral was fully restored with a visitor centre.
A camera trap showed the elusive leopard inhabiting forested areas.
Hussein Ali Mwinyi became the president of Zanzibar.
Zanzibar launched its first government-backed electric public bus service.
